bridge.done.park: A park was laid out in {district}

bridge.welcome: Welcome to {city}! Every chat with Claude is a builder in your town.
bridge.welcome.settingsHint: what to show in the world: presets and switches
preset.minimal.label: Minimal
preset.minimal.desc: Only builders and houses, like the first version.
preset.basic.label: Basic
preset.basic.desc: Tested features that don't make noise. For now that's renovation instead of demolition; more are added as they are tested.
preset.max.label: Maximum
preset.max.desc: Every tested feature. Experimental and privacy options are only switched on by hand.
feature.chronicle.label: House chronicle
feature.chronicle.desc: A lectern with a book beside every door: who built it and when, how long it worked, commits, tests. Click the sign by the door for a summary in chat and the claude --resume command.
feature.chronicleWithPrompt.label: Task text in the chronicle
feature.chronicleWithPrompt.desc: Write the start of the chat's first message (up to 200 characters) into the book and the summary. Off in every preset: the prompt text ends up in the world.
feature.callout.label: Your builder calls you
feature.callout.desc: When a chat waits for a permission or an answer: a red "!" above its head, one bell strike, a red bar at the top. Building pauses.
feature.idleCallout.label: Yellow "waiting for a task" bar
feature.idleCallout.desc: Chats that finished and wait for your next message: one quiet yellow bar for all of them, no sound. Gone with your next message.
feature.status.label: Status under the name
feature.status.desc: A line under the builder's name: what the chat is doing ("✎ editing · 64%"), whether it waits for you, whether it sleeps and for how long.
feature.toolInHand.label: Tool in hand
feature.toolInHand.desc: The builder holds what the chat is working with: a book (reading), a brush (edits), a pickaxe (commands), a compass (web), a bell (subagents).
feature.tests.label: Tests: sparks and a rain cloud
feature.tests.desc: Tests passed: green sparks and a chime; failed: smoke and a red flag on the lamp post; three failures in a row: a little rain cloud over the house.
feature.commits.label: Commit = church bell
feature.commits.desc: A successful git commit: one strike of the district church bell (or on the square) and a "+1 commit" fading above the builder.
feature.push.label: Push = PostAuto
feature.push.desc: git push: the yellow PostAuto bus drives through the streets from the house to the district square, with its three-tone horn.
feature.pr.label: PR = canton flag
feature.pr.desc: gh pr create: a new canton's flag is raised on the flagpole of the district square.
feature.apprentices.label: Apprentices
feature.apprentices.desc: Every subagent is a small helper next to the builder: Explore with a spyglass, Plan with a map. It leaves when the subagent is done.
feature.smoothBuilders.label: Smooth motion
feature.smoothBuilders.desc: Fast mode: mannequin builders glide between work spots (they ride an invisible display the client interpolates) and turn to the next block, instead of jumping.
feature.realTime.label: Real day and night
feature.realTime.desc: World time follows your clock: night in town at night, sunrise in the morning. Updated once a minute.
feature.windows.label: Lights in the windows
feature.windows.desc: The house a working chat is building has its lights on. At night you see at a glance who is working.
feature.chimney.label: Chimney smoke
feature.chimney.desc: While a chat works, a tall column of smoke rises from its house's chimney; when it idles, the chimney is cold.
feature.advancements.label: Advancements
feature.advancements.desc: Pop-up achievements for the town's milestones: the first house, the night shift, a green light after three test failures, a hive of five subagents…
feature.economy.label: Chat economy
feature.economy.desc: A short chat places a bench, a tree or a fountain on the square; its own house comes after 20 actions and grows in stages. Long chats build public works: a church, a tower, a park, then a forest and a lookout on the summit.
feature.renovation.label: Renovation instead of demolition
feature.renovation.desc: When the blueprints change, finished houses are repaired by the difference: the district's free builders change only what changed.
feature.adaptive-terrain.label: Town follows the terrain
feature.adaptive-terrain.desc: New plots climb the hillside in terraces with stone retaining walls instead of flattening it, never build on water or cliffs, and are linked by stair lanes; viewpoints appear at cliff edges. A new city is founded in a valley with a lake or river and hills around.
feature.waterfront.label: Lake front
feature.waterfront.desc: Where the town meets the water: quays with railings, lamps and benches, jetties with boats, a promenade or a lido with parasols, and a harbour with a breakwater and a lighthouse.
feature.river-bridges.label: Bridges over rivers
feature.river-bridges.desc: A district may grow across a river: a stone arch bridge, a covered wooden bridge with flower boxes and a water tower, or a viaduct over a gorge.
feature.shore-renovation.label: Quays for existing plots
feature.shore-renovation.desc: Additive renovation of the existing town: grass slopes that run into the water get a stone quay with steps, railings, lamps and benches, open water a jetty, the best bay a harbour. Nothing is demolished.
feature.allay.label: Web search = mail allay
feature.allay.desc: WebSearch/WebFetch: an allay flies off from the builder to fetch a "letter" and comes back after 4 seconds. At most once every 10 seconds.
feature.compact.label: Compaction = coffee break
feature.compact.desc: The chat compacts its memory: the builder sits down with a mug for a few seconds, and people nearby see "chat compacted its memory".
feature.storm.label: API limit = mountain storm
feature.storm.desc: A chat hit a rate limit or an overload: a thunderstorm for a minute, lightning strikes only the far peaks. At most once every 5 minutes.
feature.planMode.label: Plan mode = architect
feature.planMode.desc: In plan mode the builder holds a map, and the outline of the future house sparkles at its corners. Building starts after leaving plan mode.
feature.professions.label: Villagers by house type
feature.professions.desc: A farmer moves into the farm, a cleric into the church, a butcher into the café, a librarian into the hotel. The farm gets a cow and a goat; now and then a cowbell rings.
feature.scaffolding.label: Scaffolding
feature.scaffolding.desc: While a house is being built, scaffolding rises at its corners; it comes down with the fireworks at the end.
feature.alphorn.label: Alphorn at the finish
feature.alphorn.desc: When a house is finished, the low sound of an alphorn rolls through the valley.
feature.quirks.label: Little things
feature.quirks.desc: rm -rf: the builder holds dynamite for a second (no explosion); the hard hat depends on the model (Opus: gold, Haiku: leather); Ctrl+C: drops the tool.
feature.townRank.label: Settlement rank
feature.townRank.desc: A district grows with its number of houses: Weiler → Dorf (3) → Städtli (8) → Stadt (15). A new name over the square, a monument and a title on promotion.
feature.francs.label: Francs for tokens
feature.francs.desc: Over the main square, a "Kasse: CHF 12 480" board: 1 franc per 1000 tokens (only the usage numbers are read from transcripts).
feature.matterhorn.label: Matterhorn progress bar
feature.matterhorn.desc: At 10 houses a Swiss flag goes up on the nearest peak, then every 10 houses add a new ring of lanterns. Visible at night from the valley.
feature.townHall.label: Town hall
feature.townHall.desc: A window with every builder: those waiting for you on top, click to teleport. Opens from the pause menu or the [Town hall] link in chat.
feature.locatorBar.label: Builders on the locator bar
feature.locatorBar.desc: Builders show up on the locator bar; those waiting for you as a red dot. (The bar is visible in survival/adventure mode.)
feature.whileAway.label: "While you were away"
feature.whileAway.desc: When you join: how many houses and commits appeared while you were away and who is waiting for you now, with teleport links.
feature.clockBells.label: The Zytglogge strikes the hours
feature.clockBells.desc: Every hour (7 to 22) the clock tower bell strikes by real time, and a parade of little polar bears circles the tower. Quiet at night.
feature.sbbClock.label: SBB clocks
feature.sbbClock.desc: The dials of towers and churches show real hands by your time; the red second hand goes round in 58.5 s and pauses at the top for 1.5 s.
feature.holidays.label: 1 August and Christmas
feature.holidays.desc: 1 August: flags on the squares, bonfires on the peaks and fireworks at 21:00; 24–26 December: rain in the valley and snow in the mountains.
feature.residents.label: Residents with routines
feature.residents.desc: Villagers live in the houses: they sleep in their beds at night, work at the workstations by day and meet at the bell. Replaces the villager standing at the door. Their number follows the life density.
feature.seated.label: People at tables and in pews
feature.seated.desc: People sit on the café terrace by day, in the church pews on Sunday morning, at the hotel restaurant at meal times and at the family table in the evening (real clock). Static and capped.
feature.builderLife.label: The builders' day
feature.builderLife.desc: Builders wear a hi-vis vest and a hard hat, cheer when a house is done, meet at the district café after work (17–20 h) and, once their chat has been quiet for a while, sleep in their own bed instead of in the street.
feature.animals.label: Animals in their places
feature.animals.desc: Cows and a goat in the farm pasture, hens by the farmhouse, a cat at some doors, a St. Bernard at the alpine hut, bees over the flower beds, fish in the fountains, a frog on the fountain rim, rabbits in the meadows. Capped by the life density.
feature.cableCar.label: Cable car
feature.cableCar.desc: A red gondola runs on a cable from the edge of town up to the nearest peak, over pylons where the slope needs them. Moves only while somebody is in the game.
feature.train.label: Little red train
feature.train.desc: A small red train (locomotive and two coaches) loops along the streets between the main square and the district plazas and stops at each. Runs only while somebody is in the game.
feature.paragliders.label: Paragliders
feature.paragliders.desc: On fine days (9–19 h) a paraglider now and then takes off from a peak and glides down to a meadow at the edge of town in lazy S-turns. At most two in the air.
feature.boats.label: Lake steamer
feature.boats.desc: A white paddle steamer with a yellow funnel sails from the harbour's landing out onto the lake and along the piers. Needs a harbour (built by the town on a lake shore). Runs only while somebody is in the game.
feature.chatter.label: Builders chat
feature.chatter.desc: Builders now and then say a short line in the chat, like players: starting a house, waiting for your permission, red or green tests, a commit, a finished house, a coffee break, greeting each other. Rate-limited; quiet at night with real time.
param.houseAfterActions.label: Actions until its own house
param.houseAfterActions.desc: Chat economy: until this many actions, a chat places benches, trees and fountains on the district square.
param.stageActions.0.label: Actions until house stage 2
param.stageActions.0.desc: The house grows: small house → full house.
param.stageActions.1.label: Actions until house stage 3
param.stageActions.1.desc: Full house → annex and yard; after that the chat builds public works.
param.blocksPerSecond.label: Build speed, blocks/s
param.blocksPerSecond.desc: While the chat works (plus a bonus for every action).
param.renovateBlocksPerSecond.label: Renovation speed, blocks/s
param.renovateBlocksPerSecond.desc: The renovation crew, while at least one chat is working.
param.builderMode.label: Builders
param.builderMode.desc: Fast: mannequin builders, blocks appear by RCON. Realistic: one live bot player per active chat walks over from the district square and builds by hand (needs npm install in bots/; chats beyond the maximum keep a mannequin). Offline: like Fast, and while the server is off the chats keep earning their blocks, which then appear when it is back.
param.builderBotsMax.label: Live builders at most
param.builderBotsMax.desc: Realistic mode: one bot per active chat, at most this many (each bot ~30–80 MB, the runner ~230 MB; every bot also takes a player slot on the server). Other chats keep a mannequin until a bot is free.
param.botSpeed.label: Live builder pace
param.botSpeed.desc: Realistic mode: how fast bots work (fast: far blocks by RCON when a bot lags behind).
param.offlineCatchUp.label: Offline catch-up
param.offlineCatchUp.desc: Builders "offline": while the Minecraft server is off, chats earn their blocks as a backlog (at most offlineMaxBacklog per chat). When the server is back they appear as a timelapse (about offlineTimelapseSeconds, builders move as usual) or all at once.
param.lifeDensity.label: Life density
param.lifeDensity.desc: How many residents, seated people and animals the city gets (strict caps per district and for the whole city).
param.chatterFrequency.label: Builder chat
param.chatterFrequency.desc: How often builders say something in the chat.
param.colonists.label: Colonists (survival colony)
param.colonists.desc: Every active chat also gets a colonist in the survival colony on its own server (start it with wild/start-wild.cmd or node wild/colony.mjs). The city keeps building as usual.
param.colonistsMax.label: Colonists at most
param.colonistsMax.desc: One colonist per active chat, up to this many (each costs ~160 MB of RAM). Extra chats wait for a free place.
param.colonistsCaretaker.label: Caretaker colonist
param.colonistsCaretaker.desc: Keep one colonist working in the colony while no chat is active.

tune.title.dry: Promptenhorn tuning — dry run, nothing is written
tune.usage:
Usage: node tools/tune.mjs [--apply] [--profile low|medium|high] [--set <id>=<value>]... [--no-measure] [--no-client] [--json] [--lang <code>]
Without --apply it only prints the plan. Pin items by hand in config.json: "tuning": { "lock": ["server.view-distance", "builderBotsMax"] }.
tune.unknownProfile: Unknown profile {profile}: use low, medium or high.

tune.machine.line: RAM {ram} GB, available now {free} GB · {cpu}, {threads} threads · {os} · CPU load {load} %

tune.server.offline: the server is not running: the plan uses the machine only

tune.server.tick: TPS {tps} · MSPT {mspt} ms on average, {max} ms at most (last minute) · players online {players}
tune.server.chunks: loaded chunks {total} ({ticking} with ticking entities) · force-loaded {forced}
tune.server.entities: entities {all}: villagers {villagers} (with AI {ai}), mannequins {mannequins}, items {items}, tagged by Promptenhorn {tagged}

tune.budget: Memory for Promptenhorn: {budget} GB = {ram} GB − system {os} − Minecraft client {client} − Claude {claude}
tune.cost: The plan needs at most {total} GB: server {server}, bridge {bridge}, live builders (up to {builders}) {bots}, colonists (up to {colonistsN}) {colonists}

tune.changes.none: nothing to change: the setup already matches the plan

tune.flagsDropped: This Java does not know {flags}: left out.
tune.note.tooSmall: Even the smallest setup needs {need} GB but only {have} GB is left next to the client and Claude: close other programs, use --no-client if you play on another computer, or run the server on another machine.
tune.note.overloaded: The server is overloaded right now (TPS {tps}, MSPT {mspt} ms): building speed and life density come from the profile below.
tune.note.busy: The server is busy (MSPT {mspt} ms out of 50): fine, but don't raise the speeds.
tune.note.forceloads: {n} chunks are force-loaded: they tick all the time even when nobody is near.
tune.note.villagers: {n} villagers walk around with AI: turning villagerAI off saves the most tick time.
tune.note.items: {n} dropped items are lying around: they cost tick time until they despawn.
tune.now.missing: Right now {missing} GB would be missing for this plan at its peak. The biggest other users: {list}.
tune.now.ok: Right now the plan fits with {spare} GB to spare at its peak.
tune.client: Minecraft client: set the render distance to the server's view-distance or less, give it 2–3 GB in the launcher (more only makes its pauses longer) and let the launcher close after the game starts.
tune.next.dry: To write this plan: node tools/tune.mjs --apply (backups go to backups/tune/). Then restart the server and the bridge.
tune.applied.nothing: Nothing was written: everything already matches.
tune.restart.how: Restart to take effect: type "stop" in the server window, close the bridge window, then start start.cmd (Windows) or ./start.sh (macOS, Linux) again.
tune.verify: Check afterwards: "tps" and "mspt" in the server console (20 TPS, MSPT well under 50 ms), or run node tools/tune.mjs again.
